analyses.name: Bank of America Corporation
analyses.verdict: The cleanest technical setup in the market and the fundamentals earned it — a bank printing new highs on 34% EPS growth while still trading at 12x forward earnings.

financials.summary: Bank of America's last full fiscal year was a net-interest-income recovery story. The deposit-repricing squeeze that defined the prior tightening cycle eased, and the securities portfolio kept rolling out of low-coupon paper into higher-yielding assets — that combination expanded net interest margin and is the mechanism behind the 34.1% EPS growth the scan reports. A second engine ran alongside it: trading and investment banking revenue recovered as capital-markets activity reopened, giving the year a balance between spread income and fee income that the prior two years lacked. Credit behaved. Consumer charge-offs normalised toward pre-pandemic levels rather than deteriorating, and commercial-real-estate reserves proved adequate against a portfolio the market had spent two years worrying about. Expenses grew more slowly than revenue, which is the reason this re-rating has legs: it is operating leverage, not a one-off quarter. Capital generation supported both a higher dividend and sustained buybacks while CET1 stayed comfortably above regulatory minimums.
highlights: EPS +34.1% YoY — the engine behind the re-rating
Revenue +16.8% YoY, led by net interest income expansion
Forward P/E 12.0 — still a discount to the market despite the growth
Net interest margin expanded as the securities book repriced higher
Positive operating leverage: expenses grew slower than revenue
Capital return sustained through both dividend growth and buybacks

accomplishments: Returned to sustained net interest income growth after the deposit-cost squeeze
Rebuilt investment banking and trading revenue as capital markets reopened
Held consumer credit losses within normalisation rather than deterioration
Maintained CET1 well above requirements while increasing capital return
Continued digital-banking share gains, keeping cost-to-serve trending down
Reached a patent agreement with USAA, closing a long-running litigation overhang

journey_52w.summary: A textbook year-long base-and-breakout. BAC traded as low as 43.96 and now sits at 63.55 — a 45% advance — and it got there in stages rather than one spike. Most of the year was spent building a five-contraction consolidation in which each pullback was shallower than the last, the tightest only 2.5%. The 50-DMA (58.12) and 200-DMA (53.41) climbed steadily beneath price the entire time. The relative-strength line reached new highs before price did, which is the classic tell that institutions were accumulating into the base. The breakout to 63.55 completes that structure with RSI still only 64.7 — a stock at new highs that has not yet become extended.

analyses.name: Citizens Financial Group, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The best risk-adjusted entry in the bank group — 0.3% from a 52-week high with RSI at 59, growing EPS 41% and priced at 11.3x.

financials.summary: Citizens spent the last full fiscal year completing the turn from balance-sheet defence to earnings offence. Deposit costs peaked and began easing while the loan book repriced higher, and that spread widening drove the 41.3% EPS growth the scan reports on 14.7% revenue growth — a wider gap between the two than any peer here, which tells you the gain came from margin and cost discipline rather than balance-sheet expansion. The private-bank build-out, staffed largely with teams hired during the regional-banking dislocation, moved from investment phase to contribution phase and added fee income with minimal balance-sheet usage. Credit was the swing factor the market watched most closely: the general-office commercial-real-estate book, which had been the bear case for two years, was reserved down methodically without a headline loss event. Capital ratios improved through retained earnings, allowing buybacks to resume in size.

The stock reclaimed its 200-DMA (61.08) early in the run and never gave it back, and the 50-DMA (68.64) has acted as support on every pullback since. Three-month momentum of +15.5% is strong but not manic, and the relative-strength line has already made new highs. What makes the current setup unusual is the RSI: at 59.0 the stock is a third of a percent from a 52-week high yet reads as genuinely rested — buyers have absorbed supply without chasing.

analyses.name: GE Aerospace
analyses.verdict: The best large-cap industrial in the market, with the strongest TradingView confirmation of any industrial here — but RSI 73.8 means you scale in rather than chase.

financials.summary: The first clean full year of GE Aerospace as a pure-play, post-separation company, and the numbers made the case for the split. Revenue grew 21.1% and EPS 19.4%, driven overwhelmingly by the commercial engine services aftermarket rather than by original-equipment deliveries — which is exactly the mix management wanted, because spare parts and shop visits carry far higher margins than the engines themselves. The installed base of LEAP and CFM56 engines kept ageing into its highest-value service window, and shop-visit volumes rose accordingly. Original-equipment output remained constrained by the same supply-chain bottlenecks affecting the whole aerospace sector, which capped upside but also supported pricing. Free cash flow conversion was strong enough to fund both buybacks and continued investment in capacity, and the defence and propulsion segment provided a steady, less cyclical counterweight to the commercial cycle.

analyses.name: NVIDIA Corporation
analyses.verdict: The first real repair signal in the semiconductor complex — trend structure reclaimed, TradingView's strongest card in the file, and 17x forward earnings. The August 27 print is the whole risk.

financials.summary: The last full fiscal year was the one in which the AI data-centre buildout stopped being a forecast and became the bulk of the income statement. Revenue grew 85.2% and EPS 214.5% — the gap between those two numbers is the story, because it means the incremental revenue arrived at extraordinary incremental margin. Data-centre revenue, driven by the Blackwell-generation accelerator ramp, dwarfed gaming, professional visualisation and automotive combined. The constraint on the year was never demand; it was advanced packaging and high-bandwidth memory supply, which meant the order book ran ahead of shipments for most of the period. Networking — the switching and interconnect attach that comes with every large cluster — became a material second revenue line in its own right. Cash generation was large enough to fund buybacks at scale while still increasing R&D, and the balance sheet ended the year with no meaningful leverage.

journey_52w.summary: A round trip that is now resolving upward. NVDA ranged from 164.98 to 235.47 over the year and currently trades 222.63 — 5.5% below the high. The intervening period was a genuine drawdown: the whole semiconductor complex de-rated on inventory and capex-digestion fears, and NVDA fell through both major moving averages with it. What separates the last few weeks is that NVDA has reclaimed the 50-DMA (205.89) and the 200-DMA (193.61) while AMAT remains 28% off its high, MU 30%, LRCX 31% and AMD 18% with a TradingView SELL. Three-month momentum is only +5.4%, which tells you how much of this is repair rather than thrust, but the relative-strength line has turned up (+3.5% over four weeks) and TradingView's rating flipped to STRONG BUY with 17 buy signals and zero sells.

analyses.name: Dell Technologies Inc.
analyses.verdict: The AI buildout expressed through servers instead of silicon — 282% EPS growth at 20x forward earnings — with a wide, volatile base that demands smaller size.

financials.summary: The last full fiscal year turned Dell from an infrastructure company with an AI story into an AI company with an infrastructure business attached. Revenue grew 87.5% and EPS 282.5%, driven almost entirely by the Infrastructure Solutions Group shipping AI-optimised server racks to hyperscalers, neocloud providers and large enterprises. The order backlog grew faster than shipments for most of the year, constrained by GPU allocation rather than by demand or manufacturing capacity. The important nuance is margin: AI server gross margins are structurally thinner than Dell's traditional storage and PC businesses, so the revenue mix shift was dilutive to percentage margins even as it was hugely accretive to absolute dollars — which is why EPS grew three times faster than revenue only because of scale and operating leverage, not because the new business is more profitable per dollar. The Client Solutions PC business remained the stable, cash-generative counterweight, and storage returned to modest growth.

analyses.verdict: The fastest-growing large-cap on the pick list — 37% revenue growth, RS at new highs, TradingView 16 buy / 0 sell, and 90 days until the next earnings print.

financials.summary: Arista's last full fiscal year was defined by the shift from enterprise campus networking to AI back-end fabric as the dominant growth driver. Revenue grew 37.7% and EPS 35.7% — growth of that magnitude at that scale with margins essentially intact is the signature of a company selling into a supply-constrained market where it holds genuine technical differentiation. The high-radix Ethernet switching platforms became the default alternative to proprietary interconnect for large GPU clusters, and the EOS software layer remained the reason customers consolidated on the platform rather than buying on price. Gross margins held up despite component cost pressure, and the company continued to operate with no debt and a large net cash position. The concentration issue is structural and unchanged: a handful of hyperscale customers account for a disproportionate share of revenue, which is simultaneously the growth engine and the single largest risk.

analyses.name: TJX Companies, Inc. (The)
analyses.verdict: The right consumer exposure for a tape where the index is at highs but the shopper is trading down — with TradingView's perfect 16 buy / 0 sell card and an August 19 print to plan around.

financials.summary: TJX's last full fiscal year demonstrated why off-price is the most defensive model in retail: revenue grew 9.2% while EPS grew 29.3%, and that gap is the entire investment case. Comparable-store sales were driven by customer traffic rather than by price increases — the healthiest possible composition, because traffic-led comps compound while price-led comps eventually break. Merchandise margin expanded as excess inventory in the broader apparel and home markets gave TJX's buying organisation exceptional access to branded goods at attractive costs, precisely the environment the model is built to exploit. Store growth continued at a measured pace across Marmaxx, HomeGoods and the international banners, and shrink pressure, which had weighed on the whole sector, stabilised. Buybacks and dividend growth continued alongside the store expansion.

analyses.name: Digital Realty Trust, Inc.
analyses.verdict: AI infrastructure with a landlord's risk profile — 30% revenue growth and TradingView's joint-best card (17 buy / 0 sell). Judge it on FFO and leasing, not on the alarming headline P/E.

financials.summary: Digital Realty's last full fiscal year was the one in which AI demand fundamentally changed the leasing economics of the data-centre business. Revenue grew 29.9% as leasing volumes and, more importantly, renewal spreads moved sharply higher — existing tenants renewing at materially higher rates because there is simply not enough powered capacity available in the major markets. The binding constraint on the industry shifted decisively from capital or land to grid power, and DLR's portfolio of already-powered facilities in supply-constrained metros became correspondingly more valuable. The development pipeline expanded, funded through a mix of joint ventures and capital recycling rather than balance-sheet leverage alone. The headline earnings figure requires context: reported EPS was down 58.7% and forward P/E screens at 66.1, but REIT GAAP earnings are heavily distorted by depreciation on a rapidly growing asset base and by gains on asset sales in the comparison period. Funds from operations and leasing backlog are the metrics that reflect the business.

analyses.name: Eli Lilly and Company
analyses.verdict: The best fundamental growth story in large-cap healthcare — 48% revenue growth — available at RSI 51.6 while it rests 3.8% below its high.

financials.summary: Lilly's last full fiscal year was dominated by the incretin franchise: revenue grew 47.7% and EPS 26.2%, with the gap between those two figures explained by the enormous manufacturing capacity investment required to meet demand. That spending is the right kind of margin pressure — it is capacity being built for a market that remains supply-constrained rather than cost inflation on a mature product. Tirzepatide-based products in both diabetes and obesity indications drove the majority of incremental revenue, supported by steadily broadening insurance coverage as payers moved from blanket exclusion toward managed access. The Alzheimer's franchise contributed a second, smaller growth vector. Beyond the headline products, the pipeline advanced across oral incretin formulations and next-generation mechanisms, which matters because the current franchise's patent cliff, however distant, defines the terminal value debate. The balance sheet carried more debt than historically, reflecting the capacity buildout and business development.

analyses.name: Phillips 66
analyses.verdict: The most rested entry on the list — RSI 47 at 10.4x earnings with a live geopolitical catalyst — but TradingView disagrees, and an Iran deal is the specific way this trade fails.

financials.summary: Phillips 66's last full fiscal year was a crack-spread recovery year: revenue grew 56.2% and EPS 344.7%, a ratio that tells you almost everything about how refining economics work. Refining is a spread business, so when the gap between crude input costs and refined product prices widens, essentially all of the incremental revenue drops toward the bottom line. Global refining capacity has tightened structurally over the past several years as older, less complex facilities closed while replacement capacity lagged, and Middle East supply disruption during the period widened product cracks further. Beyond refining, the midstream segment provided fee-based cash flow that is far less volatile than the refining margin, and the chemicals joint venture contributed through a softer petrochemical cycle. Management continued the asset-disposal and debt-reduction programme while returning substantial cash through buybacks — the correct capital allocation at a cyclical peak, and the reason the balance sheet is stronger entering any downturn than it was entering the last one.

analyses.name: Southwest Airlines Company
analyses.verdict: The cheapest name on the list at 9.7x, resting at RSI 50 with TradingView's perfect 16 buy / 0 sell card — and a natural hedge against the refiner position.

financials.summary: Southwest's last full fiscal year was the first to reflect the largest commercial-model change in the airline's history. Revenue grew 16.4% and EPS 20.5% as assigned and premium seating, checked-bag fees and the redesigned fare structure moved from announcement to actual revenue — a set of changes that abandoned decades of differentiation in exchange for revenue streams every competitor had already monetised. The mechanics matter: these are high-margin ancillary revenues that require almost no incremental cost, so the incremental dollars flow through at very high margin, which is why EPS outgrew revenue. Unit revenue improved as the network was retimed and underperforming routes trimmed. Costs remained the harder side of the equation: labour rates stepped up under the current contracts, and aircraft delivery delays continued to constrain fleet planning and gauge upgauging. Fuel was the year's swing factor, as it always is, and the balance sheet remained one of the strongest in the industry.

analyses.verdict: A NEW LISTING with 38 days of trading history, now 48% below its post-IPO high — the quant signals are meaningless here, and the thesis has to carry the position entirely.

financials.period: FY2025 (last full fiscal year disclosed at IPO)
financials.summary: SpaceX came public only weeks ago, so the public financial record is limited to what was disclosed in the offering documents, and any per-line detail should be treated as preliminary rather than as an audited multi-year track record. What the scan does capture is revenue growth of roughly 92% — a rate driven by two distinct businesses with very different economics. The launch business is the mature side: a reusable-booster cadence no competitor approaches, generating revenue from commercial satellite customers, government and defence contracts, and crewed missions, with margins improving as reuse economics compound. The satellite-internet constellation is the larger and less proven side: it is a consumer and enterprise subscription business layered on top of an extraordinarily capital-intensive orbital asset base, with the key question being whether subscriber growth and revenue per user can outrun the replacement cycle of the satellites themselves. Free cash flow generation, launch-cadence economics and constellation capital intensity are the three numbers to demand from the first few public reports. Treat everything here as a thesis about a business rather than as a read on a seasoned income statement.
